title: Trump’s Intervention in Balogun’s World Cup Suspension Adds to Conflict With Europe
partialText: The decision to reverse a one-game ban landed badly in Europe, at a moment of already-heightened geopolitical tension with the United States.

title: As Trump Cools on NATO, Turkey Hosts Summit Meeting
partialText: As President Trump cools on the alliance, its members see Turkey’s large military and vibrant defense sector as assets.

title: Russia Strikes Kyiv, Ukraine’s Capital, on Eve of NATO Summit
partialText: Ballistic missiles were fired into the capital of Ukraine as Russia launched its second major attack in less than a week. At least 12 people were killed, officials said.

title: Ukraine Remade Air Defense, but Russia Has Changed Its Attacks
partialText: Ukraine has changed how militaries use Patriot systems. But recent attacks prove that clever adaptations cannot overcome a shortage of interceptors.

title: Turkey Hosts NATO Summit While Cracking Down on Critics
partialText: In the weeks leading up to the two-day event, the Turkish authorities blocked websites, jailed scores of people over allegations of terrorism and arrested a prominent comedian.

title: Why A.I. Distillation Has Become a Hot Topic in the Race with China
partialText: U.S. companies complain that competitors in China are unfairly copying their A.I. systems using a technique that has been around for years.

title: Alibaba’s A.I. Is a Hit, but Hard to Turn Into a Moneymaker
partialText: The Chinese company’s models have won over developers worldwide, but they are open source — so they can be used and modified freely.

title: In Trump’s Second Midterm, Democrats Are Looking for Fighters
partialText: Attitudes in the party have shifted, Democrats say, with a growing appetite for outsider candidates vowing to overhaul the system. Some worry that the trend could be costly in November.

title: Bill Frist Wants to Take Politics Out of Climate Change
partialText: Bill Frist, a surgeon who also served as Senate majority leader, has emerged as an outspoken advocate for environmental health. “A healthier planet means healthier people,” he said.

title: For Families With Nonspeaking Autistic Children, a Fierce Debate Over Assisted Spelling
partialText: Popular communication methods for nonspeaking autistic people have ignited a fierce debate over what counts as evidence of hidden cognitive abilities.

title: Nancy Ward, the Cherokee Leader, Stokes Division Even 250 Years Later
partialText: In 1776, Cherokee leaders looked for ways to navigate a foreboding future. Nanyehi, a.k.a. Nancy Ward, is venerated and reviled for her choice.

title: Efforts to Help Smokers Quit Stall Under Trump
partialText: The C.D.C.’s tobacco control office has been shut for more than a year. After its most prominent antismoking campaign went off the air, calls to 1-800-QUIT-NOW lines have plummeted.

title: Zyn’s Popularity Has Tobacco Companies Racing to Cash In
partialText: The makers of nicotine pouches are building new plants and expanding to meet demand. While influencers claim health benefits, experts warn the products can be highly addictive.

title: China Test Fires Long-Range Ballistic Missile in the Pacific
partialText: China’s firing of a submarine-launched missile came as Australia secured more defense deals with Pacific Island nations. Countries expressed concern about the test.

title: The Funeral of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
partialText: Iran’s new leaders are commemorating Ayatollah Khamenei, who was killed on the first day of the U.S.-Israeli war against the country.

title: Gas Stations Gain When Oil Prices Start to Drop
partialText: President Trump is berating gasoline retailers for keeping prices high. Evidence suggests the business has grown more profitable.

title: Ships Are Moving In and Out of the Persian Gulf, Easing Oil Prices
partialText: A recovery in oil flows from the Persian Gulf and a pledge by OPEC Plus to pump more crude have put downward pressure on energy prices.

title: Inside Bath & Body Works’ Fragrance Factory
partialText: “Japanese Cherry Blossom” has brought in $1.5 billion over the last 20 years. Can the company’s close-knit network of suppliers come up with the next big thing and improve sales?

title: Bring Back the SAT, California
partialText: Under the test-blind policy, more students are thrown into classes for which they are unprepared.

title: The Liberal American Jew’s Dilemma
partialText: Over the years, I have moved toward the way of being Jewish that my father rejected.

title: The Latest News
partialText: Catch up after the long weekend.

title: Research Universities Are Admitting Fewer Ph.D.s, a Bad Sign for Science
partialText: Some of the nation’s top research universities are shrinking doctoral programs because of uncertain federal funding.
